title.en: Lesson 1. Present Impressions: Adjectives vs Verbs

blocks.md:
In Korean, stating facts too directly (*“This is bad”*, *“It is hot”*) can sound blunt. Native speakers constantly use **-것 같아요** (*“It seems like... / I feel that...”*) to soften their speech.

In the present tense, adjectives and verbs take slightly different shapes:

1. **Adjectives** take **-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요**:
- No batchim → **-ㄴ 것 같아요** *(바쁘다 → 바쁜 것 같아요)*
- Has batchim → **-은 것 같아요** *(좋다 → 좋은 것 같아요)*
- **ㅂ irregular** → **-운 것 같아요** *(덥다 → 더운 것 같아요, 춥다 → 추운 것 같아요)*

2. **Action Verbs** take **-는 것 같아요**:
- *“창밖을 보니까 비가 오**는 것 같아요**.”* (Looking outside, it seems to be raining.)

Word
Present Impression (-것 같아요)
rows: **비가 오는 것 같아요** (Seems to be raining)
**잘 먹는 것 같아요** (Seems to eat well)

items.ch: 오늘 날씨가 조금 더운 것 같아요.
items.tip: I think the weather is a bit hot today.

items.ch: 창밖을 보니까 비가 오는 것 같아요.
items.tip: Looking outside, it seems like it’s raining.

items.ch: 이 음식이 정말 맛있는 것 같아요.
items.tip: I think this food is really delicious.

blocks.q: How do you say "It seems hot today" with 덥다 (ㅂ irregular)?
blocks.why: 덥다 is a ㅂ-irregular adjective: 덥- changes into 더운 것 같아요.

blocks.sentence: 창밖을 보니까 지금 비가 [오는 것 같아요].
blocks.meaning: Looking out the window, it seems to be raining right now.
blocks.why: Action verbs in the present take -는 것 같아요: 오- + -는 것 같아요 = 오는 것 같아요.

blocks.q: Put in order: "I think the weather is a bit hot today."

blocks.wrong: 지금 친구가 집에 오은 것 같아요.
answers: 지금 친구가 집에 오는 것 같아요.
지금 친구가 집에 오는 것 같아요
blocks.hint: Action verbs take -는 것 같아요: 오- + -는 것 같아요 = 오는 것 같아요
blocks.why: Verbs take -는 것 같아요: 지금 친구가 집에 오는 것 같아요.

blocks.q: It seems to be raining right now.
blocks.hint: 지금, 비가 오다 → 오는 것 같아요

blocks.say: 창밖을 보니까 비가 오는 것 같아요.

title.en: Lesson 2. Future & General Guesses: -(으)ㄹ 것 같다

blocks.md:
When predicting what **will happen** or guessing an outcome, use **-(으)ㄹ 것 같아요** (*“I think it will... / It seems like it will...”*):
- Stem without batchim → **-ㄹ 것 같아요** *(비가 오다 → 비가 올 것 같아요)*
- Stem with batchim → **-을 것 같아요** *(맛있다 → 맛있을 것 같아요)*

**Notice the contrast**:
- **비가 오는 것 같아요**: Looking out the window right now, raindrops are falling. *(Present observation)*
- **비가 올 것 같아요**: Looking at dark clouds or the forecast, you predict rain will come. *(Future guess)*

head: Word
Future Guess (-(으)ㄹ 것 같아요)
English Meaning
rows: I think it will be delicious (looking at menu)
I think I will be busy tomorrow
I guess the test will be difficult

items.tip: I think it will rain tomorrow.

items.ch: 이 케이크 정말 맛있을 것 같아요.
items.tip: This cake looks like it will be so delicious!
I think tomorrow’s exam will be difficult.

blocks.q: Looking at a menu photo, how do you guess "I think this will be delicious"?
blocks.why: Predicting before tasting takes -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요: 맛있을 것 같아요.

blocks.sentence: 하늘이 흐려요. 곧 비가 [올 것 같아요].
blocks.meaning: The sky is overcast. It seems like it will rain soon.
blocks.why: Predicting an upcoming event takes -ㄹ 것 같아요: 올 것 같아요.

blocks.q: Put in order: "I think the weather will be really good tomorrow."

blocks.hint: Predicting tomorrow takes -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 with ㅂ irregular: 어려울 것 같아요
blocks.why: Future guess for ㅂ-irregular 어렵다 is 어려울 것 같아요.

blocks.q: I think it will rain tomorrow.
blocks.hint: 내일, 비가 오다 → 올 것 같아요

blocks.say: 하늘이 흐려서 곧 비가 올 것 같아요.

title.en: Lesson 3. The Three Tenses of Observation

blocks.md:
Look at how the ending before **것 같아요** shifts depending on the time of the event:

- **Past observation**: You see puddles on the ground → *“비가 **온 것 같아요**.”* (It seems it rained.)
- **Present observation**: You see raindrops falling right now → *“비가 **오는 것 같아요**.”* (It seems to be raining.)
- **Future prediction**: You check tomorrow’s weather app → *“비가 **올 것 같아요**.”* (I think it will rain.)

head: Tense
Connector Form
Example Sentence
Situation
rows: Looking at wet puddles on the ground

blocks.md:
**Why do these three have different shapes?**

Notice that the small piece attached to the verb changes depending on time:

- 과거: **-(으)ㄴ**
- 현재: **-는**
- 미래: **-(으)ㄹ**

Why do these exact three shapes exist across Korean? **You will discover the astonishing secret behind this in the very next stage!** For now, simply remember how each tense sounds.

items.tip: It seems it rained yesterday. (Past observation)
It seems to be raining right now. (Present observation)
I think it will rain tomorrow. (Future prediction)

blocks.q: You see wet ground outside in the morning. Which sentence matches: "It seems it rained (earlier)"?
blocks.why: For a past action that left evidence, use -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요: 비가 온 것 같아요.

blocks.q: You see dark clouds gathering in the afternoon. Which sentence matches: "I think it will rain (soon)"?
blocks.why: For an anticipated future event, use -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요: 비가 올 것 같아요.

blocks.sentence: 바닥이 다 젖었어요. 아까 비가 [온 것 같아요].
blocks.meaning: The ground is all wet. It seems it rained earlier.
blocks.why: Evidence of a completed past action takes -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요: 온 것 같아요.

blocks.wrong: 아까 친구가 벌써 집에 갈 것 같아요.
answers: 아까 친구가 벌써 집에 간 것 같아요.
아까 친구가 벌써 집에 간 것 같아요
blocks.hint: For an action that already happened earlier (아까), use 간 것 같아요: 가- + -ㄴ 것 같아요
blocks.why: Past observation uses -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요: 아까 친구가 벌써 집에 간 것 같아요.

blocks.q: It seems to have rained earlier.
blocks.hint: 아까, 비가 오다 → 온 것 같아요

blocks.say: 바닥이 젖은 걸 보니까 비가 온 것 같아요.

title.en: Lesson 4. Softening Your Opinions in Conversation

blocks.md:
In Korean culture, directly stating an opinion or fact (like **너무 매워요** or **재미없어요**) can sometimes sound blunt or harsh.

Native speakers often use **-(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다** to soften their opinions, making their speech sound polite, modest, and considerate:

- **조금 비싼 것 같아요.** *(I think it's a bit expensive, softer than 비싸요)*
- **이 옷이 더 잘 어울리는 것 같아요.** *(I think this outfit suits you better)*
- **민수 씨가 지금 바쁜 것 같아요.** *(Minsu seems busy right now)*

Pair it with **조금** (*a little*) or **제 생각에는** (*in my opinion*)!

head: Direct (Can sound blunt)
Softened with 것 같아요 (Polite)
Nuance
rows: I think it is a bit too spicy.
I feel this one might be better.
It looks like there are a lot of people.
I don't think Minsu will make it.

items.ch: 제 생각에는 이 색이 더 예쁜 것 같아요.
items.tip: In my opinion, I think this color is prettier.
I think the size is a little bit small.
It seems the movie will start soon.

blocks.q: Your coworker asks how the new office chair is. How do you politely soften the negative critique: "I think it is a bit uncomfortable"? (불편하다 = uncomfortable)
blocks.why: 불편하다 is an adjective ending in a vowel, so attach -ㄴ 것 같아요 → 불편한 것 같아요 to politely soften the opinion.

blocks.sentence: 제 생각에는 이 식당 음식이 정말 [맛있는 것 같아요].
blocks.meaning: In my opinion, I think the food at this restaurant is really delicious.
blocks.why: 맛있다 takes -는 것 같아요 because of 있다: 맛있는 것 같아요.

blocks.q: 좋다 (to be good) / Soften your opinion: 「이 방법이 더 ___ . (I think it is better)」
blocks.why: 좋다 is an adjective ending in a consonant (받침 ㅎ), so attach -은 것 같아요: 좋은 것 같아요.

blocks.q: Which sentence sounds like a considerate and polite impression when trying on shoes?
options: 신발이 발에 딱 맞는 것 같아요.
신발이 발에 딱 맞으면 안 돼요.
blocks.why: 맞다 (to fit) takes -는 것 같아요: 딱 맞는 것 같아요 (It seems to fit just right).

blocks.q: Put the words in order: "In my opinion, this dress is prettier."

blocks.say: 제 생각에는 내일 날씨가 아주 좋을 것 같아요.
